City council approves the new river park

By Marta Keller, 12 March 2026

Share Email Print

After three hours of debate, the city council voted eleven to four on Tuesday evening to turn the old freight yard along the river into a public park, ending a dispute that has lasted almost a decade.

The plan covers twelve hectares of land, including the former loading docks, which will be kept as covered markets, and a wetland strip that engineers say will help absorb spring floods before they reach the lower town.

Supporters filled the public gallery, and several of them spoke about growing up next to a fenced lot. "My children have only ever seen that river through a chain-link fence," said one resident, who has campaigned for the park since 2017.

What happens next

Demolition of the rail sheds is expected to begin in the autumn, with the first section of the riverside path open to walkers by the end of next year, according to the planning department.

We are giving the river back to the people who live beside it, and we are doing it in a way that protects them from the water, too.

Opponents on the council argued that the land should have been sold to pay down the city's debt, and warned that maintenance costs could grow faster than the budget set aside for them.
